role: Sharpen engine juror: senior X ghostwriter and copy chief who reads JS
verdict: The engine is safe and honest where it counts. On 158 unseen lines it lost 0 facts and flipped 0 negations, left 76 of the 79 lines that should stay alone untouched, and the homepage showed exactly what the engine returned on all 24 lines I checked there (at 1440 and 390, put-back included). But on the lines that actually need work, only 51% (40 of 79) come out postable as is: 72.8% h overall, 34 o and 9 m. The misses come from false 'this would break' bail-outs, common run-ups and labels it doesn't catch, label cuts that break the line, and a few 'just'/'basically' cuts that change the meaning.
to_95: Stop the false bail-outs. In softCut, drop the 'that' after an opinion frame whatever word follows (today 'I think that in 2026, …' becomes 'That in 2026, …' and gets rejected). Exempt the 'and that's (pretty much) it' tail from the slFragN fragment check. Only say 'without it this line breaks' when a candidate really was rejected for breaking.

Catch the most common X run-ups and labels it misses today: 'one of the most important/biggest lessons I've learned is that', '(Just) a quick thread on (why)', 'A thread of', '<Noun> tip:' (it already cuts 'Pro tip:'), '<Adj> update (on X):', 'It's crazy to think (that)', 'I'm just curious,', 'I have to say', 'Just wanted to give a (huge) shoutout to'. When one matches, never say 'Nothing soft to cut'.

Guard meaning words. Keep 'just' when it means 'simply' after a modal ('you can just log off/ask/leave/say no'). Keep the 'just' in a jab ('is actually just selling': cut only 'actually'). Keep quantifier qualifiers ('basically / pretty much / almost / nearly' before every / everyone / all / nobody).
Cut a label with a colon as one piece or not at all. Never leave 'On the startup:' / 'On $ETH:'. After a leading #tag, keep the colon or move the tag to the end.
Scope the sarcasm guard. 'yet another' alone must not freeze every soft word in a sincere line, and the why must not then call 'Honestly' 'part of what you mean'.

Make every removed span visible. Words a reshape drops ('Here are', 'We just hit', a dangling 'I') need a distinct strike with put-back, or at least a 'Moved: …' receipt line. Never show 'Tap a struck word to put it back.' when nothing is struck.

Polish the explanations. Why quotes must not end mid-phrase ('…seed round led', '…PowerPoint of social', '…decided to shut') and must keep backticks balanced. A list count is not 'proof'. 'Two beats' only when there are two. Treat 'just my opinion though' as one tail. Don't contract an emphatic 'I am saying'. Don't split an 'A, B, and C' tricolon.
Then re-run a fresh unseen set of 150 or more lines, aiming for 90% or more h overall, 80% or more h on lines that need edits, 0 meaning m and 0 false whys.

issues.where: core.js softCut ('that' strip regex) + slOK/slFragN; sharpenLine unsure branch
issues.problem: Textbook fluffy lines come back 'Kept as written' with an untrue reason. #70 'I really think that most people basically just need to sleep more and eat more protein, and that's pretty much it': softCut already produces the right line ('Most people need to sleep more and eat more protein, and that's it'), but slOK rejects it (fragment count 1 vs 0). The why then says 'without it this line breaks or says something else'. In #64, 'I think that in 2026, the companies that will win are…' becomes 'That in 2026, …' because the 'that' strip only fires before a pronoun or determiner. Probes 'I think that in 5 years nobody will remember this.' and 'I think that's pretty much it for today.' fail the same way. On the homepage the four fluff chips light up and then nothing is cut, which is the first thing a visitor tests.
issues.fix: In softCut, when the removed mark is an opinion frame (I (really|just|genuinely)? (think|believe|feel)), also drop a following 'that' whatever comes next. In slFragN, don't count a closing ', and that's (pretty much|about) it' as a fragment. In the unsure branch, use 'without it this line breaks' only when a candidate actually failed slBroken or slMeanOK. Otherwise say 'Marked, not cut. Your call.'

issues.problem: Common X run-ups go unmarked, so lines stay soft or get only a token cut. Unchanged: #94 'As a designer, one of the most important lessons I've learned is that…' (why: 'Nothing soft to cut', which is untrue); the probe 'Just a quick thread on why the halving is priced in 👇'; #115 'A thread of 12 things…'; #72 'Fitness tip:' (yet 'Pro tip:' is cut); the probe 'Big update on the app:'. Barely touched: #1 'I wanted to share some of the biggest lessons…', #42 'It's crazy to think that', #104 'I'm just curious,', #63 'Just wanted to give a huge shoutout to', #86 'I have to say'. This is the main reason only 51% of the lines that need an edit reach h.
issues.fix: Add frames, each with its own why: lesson-learned ('(As a X,)? one of the (most important|biggest) lessons I've learned is that'), '(just )?a quick thread on (why)?', '^a thread of', '^\w+ tip:', '^\w+ update( on [^:]+)?:' as one label, 'it's (kind of )?crazy to think (that)?', 'I'm (just )?curious,', 'I have to say', 'just wanted to give a (huge )?shoutout to' → 'Huge shoutout to'. Show 'Nothing soft to cut' only when no frame matched.

issues.problem: Cutting the head of a label leaves a broken opener. #44 'Quick update on the startup: we've decided to shut it down.' becomes 'On the startup: we've decided to shut it down.', and the probe 'Quick update on $ETH: still holding.' becomes 'On $ETH: still holding.' In #109, '#buildinpublic update: we're now at 1,200 users…' becomes '#buildinpublic we're now at…': the colon goes with 'update' and the tag runs into the sentence (seen at 390 too).
issues.fix: Treat '<adj>? update on <X>:' as one span. Cut the whole span only if what follows stands alone and still names X (else keep it). Never output a line that starts with a bare preposition plus colon. When a label follows a leading #tag, keep the colon ('#buildinpublic: we're…') or move the tag to the end.

issues.problem: Words that carry the meaning get cut as filler. #28 'you can just log off' becomes 'you can log off.': the 'just' (= simply) is the whole point. Same in #26 'you can just ask people' and the probes 'you can just say no.' and 'you can just leave.'. Yet 'Reminder: you can just quit.' keeps it, which is inconsistent. In #133, the jab 'is actually just selling a course' becomes 'is selling a course'. In #146, 'Basically everyone I know is burned out.' becomes 'Everyone I know…', and the probe 'Pretty much every trader I know lost money in May.' becomes 'Every trader I know lost money in May.' Both turn an approximate claim into an absolute one.
issues.fix: Add guards for (can|could|should|just) + 'just' + verb meaning 'simply' (you/we/i/they can just <verb>). In 'actually just <verb>' inside a jab, cut only 'actually'. Guard (basically|pretty much|almost|nearly|practically) before (every|everyone|everybody|everything|all|no one|nobody|none).

issues.problem: A single 'yet another' anywhere marks the whole line as sarcastic and guards every intensifier and filler word. In #119 (a sincere 300-character line), 'really', 'honestly', 'actually' and 'just' are all frozen, so only 'Unpopular opinion but' goes and the line stays over 280. The why even sells opening on 'I really think that most junior developers'. In the probe 'Honestly we just shipped yet another update and it's really fast now.' nothing is cut, and the why says 'Kept “Honestly”: here it's part of what you mean, not filler.' That is untrue.
issues.fix: Count 'yet another' as sarcasm only with a second signal: a quote, a sarcasm opener (wow/great/love how/sure), a sarcasm close (truly groundbreaking, /s), or 'yet another' in the last clause. Otherwise guard only the words inside that clause.

issues.where: slExplain (reshape glue left out of cut) + home.html render() HINT
issues.problem: Words a reshape drops are never struck, so they vanish with no receipt and no way to put them back. Cases: #33 'We just hit' ('We just hit $10k MRR…' becomes '$10k MRR…'), #6 and #81 'Here are', #157 a dangling 'I', and the hero's own example 3 ('we just crossed'). On #33 the Try box shows the draft with no strikes at all under the hint 'Tap a struck word to put it back.' (screenshot work-hook/shot-1440-33.png). Every other check matched: line, say, why, strikes = cut, the Kept row and put-back on 24 lines.
issues.fix: Return the reshape-dropped spans from slExplain as moved: [{text, at}] and strike them on the page in a second style (dotted, no ember), tappable to put back. At minimum, add 'Moved “We just hit”' to the receipt and hide the 'Tap a struck word' hint when nothing is struck.

issues.problem: #0: cutting 'just' out of 'just my opinion though' leaves 'i think $SOL will outperform $ETH this cycle, my opinion though.' The orphan tail reads wrong, and the double hedge stays.
issues.fix: Treat 'just my (opinion|two cents|take|thoughts)( though| tho)?' as one tail unit: cut all of it or none. On a call, keep the 'i think' and cut the tail.

issues.problem: #83 'I'm not saying you should never use an ORM, but I am saying you should really understand…' becomes '…ORM. But I'm saying you should understand…'. Contracting the stressed 'I am' kills the contrast and reads off.
issues.fix: Skip the am/is/do contraction when the line has 'not … but <pronoun> (am|is|do)' or 'I'm not saying … I am saying'.

issues.where: contrast split; 'single' swap; marks vs cut
issues.problem: It touched lines that were already sharp. #3 splits the tricolon 'Funding is negative, OI is climbing, and price won't move.' In #47, 'every single week for 3 years' loses the emphasis the brag is built on. In #47/#68/#105/#109 the word cut was never underlined while typing (marks 0, cut 1), so the squiggle preview and the strikes disagree.
issues.fix: Don't split a comma list that ends in ', and'. Keep 'every single <day|week|month>' when the line carries a duration or count. Every cut must have been a mark first: either add 'single'/'update' to softMarks or don't cut them.

issues.problem: Why quotes stop mid-phrase or break code: '“We raised a $2.5M seed round led”', '“LinkedIn carousels are the PowerPoint of social”', '“On the startup: we've decided to shut”', '“An interesting chart I came”', '“I've been thinking about”', '“rm -rf /` isn’t a valid way”' (one backtick). That is 7 of 158 results, all shown under 'Why it hits'.
issues.fix: Never end a quote on a preposition, auxiliary, participle-before-'by', or the first noun of a compound. Balance backticks and quotes. If no clean 3–7 word clause exists, use the no-quote sentence.

issues.problem: 'Number first' says a list count 'reads as proof' ('“5 things” comes first…', '“10 VS Code” comes first…'). A count isn't proof, and '10 VS Code' is a broken quote. In #116, 'Split it into two beats' is said of a line that now has three sentences.
issues.fix: When the leading number counts list items (N things/tips/books/tools/extensions/lessons/mistakes), say 'The count comes first, so people know what they're getting' and quote 'N <noun>'. In the receipt, count the beats ('Split it into three beats') or say 'Split it up'.

issues.problem: #151 'we just crossed 1 million downloads' shows no Kept row. The engine's kept list is empty, and the page also drops a bare '1'. Separately, 'Kind of a big day' (a playful understatement) becomes the stilted 'A big day:'.
issues.fix: Have slFacts capture '<number> (thousand|million|billion) <noun>' as one fact. Guard 'kind of a big (day|deal)' as an idiom.

issues.problem: #122 'purple elephant spreadsheet tomorrow banana' (5 words, no verb or function word) is 'clean' with 'Nothing soft to cut, and no safe move makes it stronger', which implies it's a fine post. The word-salad rule starts at 6 words.
issues.fix: Lower the word-salad threshold to 4 or more words with no function word, verb or fact.

issues.problem: #117 trims four intensifiers, but the news ('We're officially profitable as of this month.') stays buried after a 280-character thank-you and the line stays over 280. #119 also stays over 280.
issues.fix: When a draft is over 280 and a short closing sentence holds the result or news, try 'payoff first' (move that sentence to the front) as a candidate before the 'can split into a thread' note.

issues.problem: 'I think' is kept as stance on a ticker call (#0, IMO probes) but cut on '…why I think the halving is already priced in' (#14), a market call without a ticker, while the real fluff 'Just a quick thread on why' stays. #9 keeps 'In my humble opinion,' on top of 'probably'.
issues.fix: Make isCall recognise market-structure claims (priced in, halving, top/bottom, rotation, ATH) without a ticker. When the call already carries a hedge ('probably', 'might'), let the outer opinion frame go.

issues.problem: #137: a standalone 'This is not financial advice.' is underlined as fluff, and the why says 'without the soft words there's too little left to post. Add the detail.' That nudges a trader to treat a disclaimer as filler.
issues.fix: Never mark an NFA or disclaimer sentence. On a disclaimer-only line, return clean with 'A disclaimer. Nothing to cut.'
